mathgap.title: Signed Difference Interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement mentions 'the difference between the number of X and Y', interpret it as the signed subtraction X - Y, preserving the order as stated.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement refers to the difference between two persons' counts.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'the difference between Alice and Bob' as |Alice - Bob| (absolute value) instead of Alice - Bob.

mathgap.title: Directed More-Than Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Translate statements of the form 'A has N more than B' (including combined forms) into the equation A = B + N, preserving direction.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement says one person has a certain number more than another.
mathgap.example: Treating 'Alice has 5 more than Bob' as Alice = Bob - 5 (reversing the direction).

mathgap.title: Sequential Transfer Application
mathgap.principle: When processing a transfer statement, immediately subtract the transferred amount from the giver and add it to the receiver, respecting the order of statements.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement describes a transfer of items from one person to another.
mathgap.example: Delaying a transfer until after processing all other statements, instead of applying it immediately.

mathgap.title: Immediate Direct Assignment Update
mathgap.principle: When encountering a direct count statement, set the person's count to the given number at that point, overwriting any previous value.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement directly assigns a count to a person.
mathgap.example: Keeping an earlier direct count for a person unchanged after a later direct count statement, instead of overwriting it.

mathgap.title: Preserve Difference Order
mathgap.principle: When equating a 'has more than' difference to a 'difference between' two persons, preserve the order of subtraction as stated (i.e., X - Y = A - B).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement sets one signed difference equal to another signed difference.
mathgap.example: Swapping the order to D - C when the statement says the difference between C and D.

mathgap.title: Redistribute Equally Between Two Persons
mathgap.principle: When two persons redistribute their items to ensure each has an equal amount, set each person's count to half of the combined total.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement says 'A and B redistribute their items to ensure each has an equal amount'.
mathgap.example: After redistribution, setting each person's count to the original count of one of them instead of half the total.

mathgap.title: Temporal Evaluation of Relational Statements
mathgap.principle: When evaluating a relational statement, use the current counts of the persons at that point in the text, after any prior statements have been applied.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a relational statement (e.g., 'A has N more than B') appears.
mathgap.example: Evaluating a relational statement using the initial counts of persons, ignoring updates from earlier statements.

mathgap.title: Conditional Transfer Application
mathgap.principle: When encountering a conditional transfer, first evaluate the condition using the current count, and if true, perform the transfer immediately.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement includes a conditional transfer like 'If X has more than N items, X will give them to Y'.
mathgap.example: Ignoring the condition and always performing the transfer, regardless of whether the condition holds.

mathgap.title: Combined Sum Equality Interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement gives a combined total for several persons, interpret it as the sum of those persons' counts equals the given number.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement says 'The combined quantity of X, Y, and Z is N' (or similar).
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'The combined total of A, B, and C is 10' as A = 10, B = 0, C = 0, instead of A + B + C = 10.

mathgap.title: Split Equally Among Recipients (Additive)
mathgap.principle: When a person splits all their items equally among recipients, set the donor's count to 0 and add half of the donor's original count to each recipient's current count (do not replace the recipients' existing counts).
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement says 'X splits all the Y they own equally among A and B (or more recipients)'.
mathgap.example: After 'Elizabeth splits all her 24 tomatoes equally among Jerry and Osie', setting Jerry's count to 12 and ignoring his previous 2 tomatoes, instead of adding 12 to his existing count.

mathgap.description: Interpreting 'difference between X and Y' as absolute value instead of signed subtraction.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model defaults to thinking of 'difference' as a magnitude, forgetting the order matters in signed equations.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always treat 'difference between X and Y' as X - Y, preserving the order given in the statement.

mathgap.description: Applying all transfers after processing other statements, ignoring their sequential effect.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats transfers as a batch operation rather than as immediate updates.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Process each transfer in the order it appears, updating counts immediately.

mathgap.description: Assuming 'A has N more than B' implies A > B and discarding solutions where the computed difference is negative.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model interprets 'more than' as a strict inequality and rejects negative differences.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat 'A has N more than B' as a signed equation A = B + N, allowing the difference to be negative if required by other constraints.

mathgap.description: Treating a direct count statement as an immutable initial value and not updating it after earlier transfers.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes the initial assignment is permanent, overlooking later modifications.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When a direct count appears, overwrite the person's current count at that point, even if earlier transfers have changed it.

mathgap.description: Evaluating relational statements using outdated counts (e.g., initial values) instead of the current counts after prior statements.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model fails to track the evolving state of each variable through the sequence of statements.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Maintain a running table of current counts and always use the latest values when evaluating any relational statement.
